architecture-decision-review.title: Architecture decision review
architecture-decision-review.purpose: Review a system design or decision for boundaries, coupling, data ownership, failure modes, reversibility, and measured properties against the project's confirmed invariants, then record the findings and raise decisions that belong to the person.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Compare stated boundaries with the code's imports and the data's owners
Review the design against its obligations
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

checkpoints: Save the first useful artifact during the first authorized write step.
Preserve partial work and unknowns before gathering or repairs exhaust their budget.
evidenceObligations: Support factual conclusions with admitted project evidence.
Inspect the actual result against the frozen acceptance criteria.
Render and inspect visual artifacts when the requested result has a visual surface.
stopWhen: Budget exhausted: preserve partial work and remaining actions.
Required permission or essential intent is unresolved.

delivery-plan-review.title: Delivery plan review
delivery-plan-review.purpose: Review a plan or status for claims that cannot all hold, the critical path, capacity as a range with assumptions, risks with owners, and decisions needed; deterministic conflict checks run first, every finding is cited, and conflicts are raised to their owners.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Run the deterministic conflict checks: dates against dependencies, double allocation, unstaffed dependencies
Review the plan against its obligations
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

experience-review.title: Experience review
experience-review.purpose: Review a screen or flow for task success, accessibility against WCAG 2.2, error states, consistency with the declared design system, and the evidence behind behavior claims; findings are recorded and unsupported claims are handed over as assumptions.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Check criterion ids, evidence refs, and error-state coverage
Review the experience against its obligations
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

governance-issue-spotting.title: Governance issue spotting
governance-issue-spotting.purpose: Spot compliance, legal, and finance issues in a change, contract, data flow, or money flow: locate and quote the governing texts, state exposures and how they may apply as research, list expected controls and existing evidence, and prepare the questions and material a qualified reviewer needs; never advice or sign-off.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Check that every exposure cites a text by section and the memo carries its label
Issue-spot against the governing texts and prepare the reviewer packet
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

implementation-review.title: Implementation review
implementation-review.purpose: Review a change, migration, or dependency proposal for correctness evidence, scope, reversibility, dependencies, and operability, cited against the project's confirmed principles; findings are recorded and anything that belongs to another pack or to the person is handed over.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Run the project's own checks and record their results
Review the implementation against its obligations
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

operational-readiness-review.title: Operational readiness review
operational-readiness-review.purpose: Review a service or change for objectives, signals, on-call, runbooks, rollback, and capacity against the project's risk posture, citing configs and records; anything without a way to notice failure and a way back is reported as not ready.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Check that objectives, alerts, and runbooks cite configs and records
Review readiness against its obligations
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

product-requirements-review.title: Product requirements review
product-requirements-review.purpose: Review a product document or proposal for problem, users, outcome and measure, scope, priority evidence, and assumptions against the project's confirmed outcome and sources, recording findings and handing the build-or-not question to the person.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Check every claim for a declared source and every outcome for a measure
Review the document against its obligations
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

security-privacy-review.title: Security and privacy review
security-privacy-review.purpose: Defensive review of a system or change: threat model per boundary, access paths, secrets, data classification and retention, dependency advisories, and detection, each finding citing its path and control; fatal exposures are raised immediately and regulatory questions handed to governance-risk.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Check that every finding names a path, a control status, and a citation
Review the target against its security and privacy obligations
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

strategy-execution-review.title: Strategy-to-execution and capacity review
strategy-execution-review.purpose: Compare strategy documents to active work and capacity: normalize initiatives, owners, dates, dependencies, allocations, constraints, skills, operational load, and throughput history with each claim's source authority; run deterministic conflict checks first, then a cited semantic review; state capacity as ranges with assumptions; deliver conflicts, unlinked work, infeasible commitments, capacity ranges, and recommended decisions with freshness and assumptions shown.

steps.title: Read the governing material and the target
Normalize the sources and run the deterministic conflict checks
Semantic review: incompatible commitments, cited to both texts
Record findings and raise what belongs to the person

prd-authoring.title: Write a PRD
prd-authoring.purpose: Write a product requirements document grounded in the project's sources and work items, in the project's template when one is named; surface conflicts and unknowns instead of resolving them silently; challenge the draft before handing it back.

steps.title: Read the governing material, sources, and work items; name every conflict between them
Write the PRD to the target file, grounded in what was gathered
Challenge the PRD: unsupported claims, silently resolved conflicts, invented owners or decisions
Record the result and hand it back

proposal-authoring.title: Write a proposal
proposal-authoring.purpose: Write a decision proposal or business case for a named reader, grounded in strategy, goals, and evidence, ending in the decision needed, from whom, and by when; challenge the draft before handing it back.

steps.title: Read the governing material, sources, and work items; name every conflict between them
Write the proposal to the target file, grounded in what was gathered
Challenge the proposal: unsupported claims, silently resolved conflicts, invented owners or decisions
Record the result and hand it back

rfc-authoring.title: Write an RFC
rfc-authoring.purpose: Write a technical RFC or design document grounded in the project's decisions, work items, and evidence; carry superseded and conflicting decisions explicitly; challenge the draft before handing it back.

steps.title: Read the governing material, sources, and work items; name every conflict between them
Write the RFC to the target file, grounded in what was gathered
Challenge the RFC: unsupported claims, silently resolved conflicts, invented owners or decisions
Record the result and hand it back

research-brief.title: Research a question
research-brief.purpose: Answer a question from the project's sources and the web the host can read, with every finding cited, sources that disagree set side by side, figures traced to where they come from, and what could not be established said plainly; challenged before it is handed back.

steps.title: Find and read what bears on the question, inside the project and out; note where sources disagree
Save the requested draft, then answer what holds, how sure, what it rests on and what remains unknown
Challenge the answer: single-source claims, stale or superseded sources, figures without a trail, conclusions the evidence does not reach
Record the answer and hand it back
